_doc: Landmark buildings (src/buildings.js landmark()): drawn from an architectural description instead of a footprint and a fitted roof, in place of the footprints they replace (by OSM / Microsoft id). Each landmark has a frame (origin in level metres, ang_deg: the direction of its u axis, degrees from +x toward +z); parts are in (u, v) metres in that frame, heights in metres above the ground at ground_at (local u, v). Part types: block (rect, walls y0..y1, roof hip/gable/deck/mansard/flat, dormers), arc (round bay: centre c, radius r, angles from -v clockwise; cap, rail), bays (pavilions along a wall with front gables and balconies), balconies, porch, rail, chimney, flagpole, bar (a long building along a polyline), seawall (level coordinates, follows the ground). story0 shifts a wall's window storeys (its first storey starts there). Colours are named from the palette, each sampled from a photograph (source and pixel listed).

palette._method: Pixel means (7x7) from Matt's photographs, divided by the photo's own white (the 99.5th-percentile brightest pixels on the white trim: photo 1 inn (223,228,233), lodge (210,225,235); photo 2 (238,240,236)) and scaled to 0.92 for white paint. Sunlit faces where there are any; shaded ones raised by the photo's own sun/shade ratio (1.8, the inn wall lit vs shaded).

landmarks.name: Bar Harbor Inn — main inn
landmarks._ref: OSM way 369089643 (the round dining room is the arc at its north face); photos 1 and 2: granite plinth, a round glazed dining room with a railed deck above, a recessed round second storey, a front gable over it, a hip roof cut flat for the widow's walk and its flagpole, gable dormers, a brick chimney, a covered veranda on the west.

landmarks.name: Bar Harbor Inn — Oceanfront Lodge
landmarks._ref: the east wing of OSM way 369089643; photo 1: three storeys in grey clapboard, nine white balcony bays on the water face, each with a front gable and balconies on three levels, a dark roof hipped at the east end
landmarks._ground: ground floor at the lawn just above the main inn's granite plinth (photo 1); the survey under the wing reads 9.9-10.2, the building's own bulk in the surface

landmarks.name: Bar Harbor Inn — Newport building
landmarks._ref: OSM way 369089637; photo 2: a long white three-storey wing following the shore, continuous balconies on all three levels on the water face, a light grey hip roof

landmarks.name: Shore Path seawall at the Bar Harbor Inn
landmarks._ref: photo 2: pale concrete retaining wall under the Shore Path from the Inn pier to the Newport building; line from OSM way 164089143 (Shore Path)
landmarks._fp: a token footprint: the wall follows the ground itself; a real one would keep trees off the whole Inn grounds
landmarks._off: drawn as a structure now (structures.json, tools/structures.py)

landmarks.name: The Turrets (College of the Atlantic)
landmarks._ref: OSM way 1162522084 (outline; its two arcs are the round towers, fitted: (-1586.0, 569.9) r 3.66 and (-1588.7, 591.1) r 3.06); lidar ridge 17.3 m over the lowest corner; Matt's photos (aerial of the west front, the sea front from the lawn). 1895 granite cottage: two storeys of rusticated pink-buff granite, a steep slate roof cut flat at the top, round towers with conical slate roofs and copper finials, a north wing set at an angle with its own hip roof, a flat-roofed entrance porch with a balustrade on the west, a veranda on a granite terrace toward the sea, granite chimneys, gable dormers.

landmarks.name: Kaelber Hall (College of the Atlantic)
landmarks._ref: OSM way 1162522080 (28.6 x 16 m); lidar ridge 15.3 m over the lowest corner; Matt's harbour aerial: two storeys in weathered cedar shingle, grey hip roofs with gable dormers, a cedar-shingled gable pavilion on the sea front, the dining room glazed on the ground floor under a porch whose roof is a deck, a brick chimney, a stone terrace.

landmarks.name: Bass Harbor Head Light
landmarks._ref: 1858 (Commons photos and the historic aerial): a short white brick tower on the granite cliff, a wide solid black gallery with a round railing, an octagonal lantern with a red lens, a dome, ball and tall rod; a short gabled passage to the 1-1/2 storey keeper's house (red roof, dormers, granite foundation) and its ell; the bell house (hip roof) east; brick oil house and barn up the drive (OSM).

landmarks.name: Baker Island Light
landmarks._ref: 1855 tower (Commons photos): cylindrical, its whitewash peeling to grey stone, a bracketed black gallery with railing and an octagonal lantern, dome and ball; the 1-1/2 storey clapboard keeper's house a few metres away with a grey cedar roof, one front dormer, a centre chimney and a rear ell, on a granite foundation; the red-brick oil house with a lichened roof and a little ventilator cupola. Acadia National Park.

landmarks.name: Bear Island Light
landmarks._ref: 1889 (Commons photos): a short white tower on the cliff top over Northeast Harbor, black gallery and ten-sided lantern with dome and ball, an attached gable workroom; the 1-1/2 storey keeper's house with a big grey cedar gambrel roof, a front dormer, two chimneys and navy-blue window trim; the barn up the path.

landmarks.name: Winter Harbor Light (Mark Island, Frenchman Bay)
landmarks._ref: 1856 (Commons photos): on pink granite: a short white tower with a black lantern and railing at one end; a one-storey workroom, a 1-1/2 storey ell with a porch on its sea side, and the two-storey keeper's house with its gable to the sea and a centre chimney; grey roofs; a dark grey shed apart. Inactive since 1933, private.

landmarks.name: Deer Isle Thorofare Light (Mark Island)
landmarks._ref: 1857 (Commons photos): a square white brick tower with a square gallery and railing and an octagonal black lantern, on the wooded point of Mark Island; its keeper's house burned in 1959 and the rest was removed, so the tower stands alone.

landmarks.name: Egg Rock Light
landmarks._ref: 1875 (photos 18 Oct): a square white tower rising out of the middle of a square 1-1/2 storey clapboard keeper's house on a grey granite foundation; the hip roof red-orange with lichen, on each face a wide dormer of four windows between two small gables; the square gallery with a square railing on the tower top, an octagonal black lantern on a tall black base, a conical dome and a large ball; front steps; a lean-to on the east; the white fog-signal house (1904) with a lichened hip roof on a concrete platform and a solar array beside it.

landmarks.name: Great Duck Island Light
landmarks._ref: 1890 (photos 18 Oct): a white cylindrical tower, a ten-sided black lantern on a bracketed gallery with a round railing and a red mast light; the white workroom west of it with a weathered red hip roof; the red-brick fog-signal house with a weathered red hip roof south of it; the 1890 keeper's house, 2-1/2 storeys of weathered white clapboard with its gable end to the sea, up the path to the north (OSM and the aerial); solar arrays east of the tower; a shed. COA's research station.

landmarks.name: Mount Desert Rock Light
landmarks._ref: 1847 (photos 18 Oct): a conical granite tower in weathered brown-grey blocks with a flared cap under the gallery, a door and small windows; the bracketed gallery, round railing and black ten-sided lantern with a dome, ball and an antenna mast; the keeper's house (1892), 2-1/2 storeys of white clapboard with a grey gable roof, a front cross gable, a dormer and a brick chimney, a porch on its west end and front, a two-storey gable-fronted wing toward the tower with solar panels on its roof and a short covered way to the tower; a solar array east of the tower; on bare, slabby granite.

landmarks.name: Mount Desert Rock boathouse and slip
landmarks._ref: The white gable-fronted boathouse at the water's edge with its timber slip down the slabs below low water (photos 18 Oct). The slip is solid: a Zodiac lands on it (world.js W.slips; Boats: trim, skeg and prop, wind and stream).

landmarks.name: Petit Manan Light
landmarks._ref: 1855 (Commons photos): a very tall, slender conical tower of tan granite blocks with small windows up its height, a bracketed black gallery and lantern; a small white hip-roofed oil house at its foot, a flagpole; the white 1-1/2 storey keeper's house gable-on to the sea and a long low grey hip-roofed building along the island.

landmarks.name: Prospect Harbor Point Light
landmarks._ref: 1891 (Commons photos): a small conical white tower with a black gallery and octagonal lantern; the 1-1/2 storey keeper's house beside it with a charcoal roof, a cross gable and dormers, dark window trim, two red chimneys, an ell. Navy-owned.

landmarks.name: Burnt Coat Harbor Light (Hockamock Head)
landmarks._ref: 1872 (Commons photos and the historic aerial): a square tower, its white paint weathering to grey, with a square gallery and railing and an octagonal lantern, joined by a covered walkway to the two-storey keeper's house (charcoal roof) and its ell; a brick oil house. Swans Island; the town keeps it.

landmarks.name: Blue Hill Bay Light (Green Island)
landmarks._ref: 1857: a short white brick tower with its attached keeper's house on tiny Green Island; decommissioned 1933, private (no photographs on Commons: from the description). The active light (Fl G 4s) is on a skeleton tower on the island.

landmarks.name: Eagle Island Light
landmarks._ref: 1858 (Commons photos): a rough whitewashed rubble tower, slightly conical, a door up a short wooden stair, a black gallery and ten-sided lantern; the tall white pyramidal bell tower beside it. The keeper's house is gone. East Penobscot Bay.

landmarks.name: Saddleback Ledge Light
landmarks._ref: 1839 (Commons photos): a conical tower of dark rough granite on a bare ledge in Isle au Haut Bay, a bracketed gallery with railing and a lantern; the frame keeper's house that once leaned on it is gone.

landmarks.name: Isle au Haut Light (Robinson Point)
landmarks._ref: 1907 (Commons photos): a 'sparkplug' tower: a granite base of dressed blocks to about 4.6 m with a white brick shaft above, a black gallery and octagonal lantern, reached from the shore by a long white wooden footbridge on posts; the Victorian keeper's house up the bank (white, charcoal roof, red chimney).

landmarks.name: Pumpkin Island Light
landmarks._ref: 1854 (Commons photos): a short white tower with a black gallery and octagonal lantern, joined by a little hip-roofed link to the 1-1/2 storey cape (grey cedar roof, one front dormer, a red chimney) and its ell; a small red shed. Eggemoggin Reach; decommissioned 1933, private.

landmarks.name: College of the Atlantic pier
landmarks._ref: Matt 19 Oct, four photographs; tools/coa_pier.py. The deck, piles, gangway and float are the dock (docks.json (coa_pier)); this is the teal rails, the arch, the benches and lamps on the fixed pier.

landmarks.name: Ticket shacks, Harborview Park
landmarks._ref: tools/waterfront_photos.py: Commons "Bar Harbor, Maine, USA18.jpg" and "USA21.jpg"; OSM Harborview Park 1365123520. Places approximate.

landmarks.name: Bar Harbor Inn pier (the Margaret Todd's pier)
landmarks._ref: tools/inn_pier.py: USGS 3DEP lidar and Matt's photograph (docs/look/photo_inn_pier_porcupines.jpg). The gangway and floats are the dock (docks.json bar_harbor_ferry_pier); this is the fixed walkway, its piles and the booth.

landmarks.name: Former Golden Anchor restaurant
landmarks._ref: Assets, site 1 item 21 (survey 4.16): corners from the lidar and two aerials; floor +3.3 (level with the pier neck, ASSUMED), roof +8.4, plant +8.9; one storey, glazed walls in a white frame, a deep sloped fascia, a flat white roof. The former Golden Anchor restaurant (BDN 2011), not a glass pavilion. Harborside point (Assets, 1 Nov; tools/harborside_point.py)
